answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because willow only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, dawn is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any basalt approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
